**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Affected part: Corn leaves
- Lesion features: Very long, elongated tan/brown necrotic streaks running parallel to leaf veins, spanning most of the leaf length
- Multiple leaves affected with similar elongated, water-soaked to tan/brown lesions
- No distinct spore pustules, circular spots, or ear involvement

**Candidate Narrowing:**
- **Goss's wilt**: Long tan/brown streaks parallel to veins — matches closely
- **Stewart's wilt**: Pale green/yellow streaks — doesn't match (these are brown/necrotic)
- **Southern Corn Leaf Blight**: Tan rectangular lesions bounded by veins — possible but lesions here are longer/more irregular

**Reference Comparison (Goss_wilt):**
The reference shows the same hallmark long, tan-brown streaks running parallel to leaf veins. The test image matches this pattern very well — elongated necrotic lesions that run the length of the leaf with irregular margins, characteristic of Goss's bacterial wilt.

This matches Goss's wilt (bacterial wilt caused by Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. nebraskensis) which produces characteristic water-soaked to tan/brown lesions that run the length of the leaf parallel to veins, distinguishable from Southern Corn Leaf Blight (more rectangular, vein-bounded lesions) and Stewart's wilt (pale green/yellow coloration)."}
